quasi_biennial_oscillation.caption: A weather balloon released from USS Kitty Hawk over the Pacific, July 2008. Balloon instruments measure winds aloft; the QBO itself is identified from long records of equatorial stratospheric winds.

blocking_pattern_persistence.alt: A dry, stony river channel runs between dense green banks.
blocking_pattern_persistence.caption: The River Mole’s dry bed near Leatherhead, England, July 2022. Drought offers context for prolonged weather patterns; the photograph alone cannot identify atmospheric blocking.

humidity_amplification.alt: A refuge worker in a yellow shirt swings a handheld weather instrument in an open field.
humidity_amplification.caption: Mary Elliott measures relative humidity with a sling psychrometer before a prescribed burn at Patuxent Research Refuge, April 2012. Field measurement makes atmospheric moisture tangible.
humidity_amplification.credit: Sandy Spencer / US Fish and Wildlife Service

ozone_formation_pressure.alt: The Los Angeles skyline fades into thick haze above a dense cityscape.
ozone_formation_pressure.caption: Hollywood and downtown Los Angeles viewed through smog in 1984. The scene provides context for urban air pollution; ozone itself is invisible and cannot be quantified from haze.

jet_stream_volatility.alt: A slanting cloud band crosses snow-covered mountain ranges beneath Earth’s curved blue horizon.
jet_stream_volatility.caption: An astronaut photograph over western Canada, December 2015, shows a long cloud band that NASA describes as a likely remnant of the polar jet. One view does not establish jet-stream volatility.
jet_stream_volatility.credit: Image courtesy of the Earth Science and Remote Sensing Unit, NASA Johnson Space Center

smoke_exposure_burden.alt: A photographer wearing a mask works among rocks beneath a dense yellow-brown smoke haze.
smoke_exposure_burden.caption: A masked photographer observes smoke from California’s Apple Fire at Eureka Peak. The smoke-filled air provides direct context for exposure risk.

aerosol_cooling_loss.alt: A researcher wearing a headset adjusts a rack of instruments inside a research aircraft.
aerosol_cooling_loss.caption: Francesca Gallo operates the LARGE aerosol instrument aboard NASA’s P-3 during the 2025 Student Airborne Research Program. Measurements help study particles that influence clouds and climate.

gas_power_dependence.alt: Tall turbine exhaust structures rise above a power station in warm evening light.
gas_power_dependence.caption: Gas-fired generating equipment at Braemar Power Station, Australia. The plant illustrates infrastructure reliant on natural gas; emissions are not visible in the photograph.

steel_decarbonization_gap.alt: Brilliant orange molten material pours from a dark furnace amid flying sparks.
steel_decarbonization_gap.caption: Iron and slag flow from a blast-furnace tap hole. This high-temperature process provides context for the challenge of replacing carbon-intensive steelmaking.

critical_mineral_extraction_pressure.alt: Workers carry and fill sacks among exposed rock faces in an open cobalt mine.
critical_mineral_extraction_pressure.caption: Artisanal cobalt extraction in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, documented by the International Institute for Environment and Development. Workers and excavated ground make the labour and land demands of mineral supply visible.
critical_mineral_extraction_pressure.credit: The International Institute for Environment and Development

battery_supply_chain_pressure.alt: Geometric green evaporation ponds border a turquoise salt lake in a dry mountain basin.
battery_supply_chain_pressure.caption: Evaporation ponds beside Gas Hure Lake, Qinghai, photographed from the ISS in September 2024. Its mineral-rich brines include lithium; the image illustrates extraction infrastructure rather than a supply shortage.
battery_supply_chain_pressure.credit: Astronaut photograph ISS071-E-715148 was acquired on September 22, 2024, with a Nikon Z9 digital camera using a focal length of 400 millimeters. It is provided by the ISS Crew Earth Observations Facility and the Earth Science and Remote Sensing Unit, Johnson Space Center. The image was taken by a member of the Expedition 71 crew. The image has been cropped and enhanced to improve contrast, and lens artifacts have been removed. The International Space Station Program supports the laboratory as part of the ISS National Lab to help astronauts take pictures of Earth that will be of the greatest value to scientists and the public, and to make those images freely available on the Internet. Additional images taken by astronauts and cosmonauts can be viewed at the NASA/JSC Gateway to Astronaut Photography of Earth. Caption by Wilfredo García López/Jacobs-JETS II Contract at NASA-JSC.

renewable_curtailment_losses.alt: Rows of wind turbines and electricity pylons share a broad open landscape.
renewable_curtailment_losses.caption: Wind turbines stand beside high-voltage transmission lines near Rye, England. The generators and grid are visible together; this scene provides context and does not establish that output was curtailed.

freight_electrification_gap.alt: A bright green-and-white delivery truck travels along a road with a charging rail embedded in its surface.
freight_electrification_gap.caption: An electric truck uses the eRoadArlanda dynamic-charging test road in Sweden, May 2019. Demonstration infrastructure illustrates one route toward freight electrification.

port_heat_vulnerability.alt: Rows of coloured shipping containers and cranes fill an open paved port yard.
port_heat_vulnerability.caption: An open container yard at Vostochny port near Nakhodka, Russia. Exposed paved working areas provide context for port heat vulnerability; this image does not document a heat incident.

species_range_compression.alt: A small pika sits on sunlit rocks beside low alpine vegetation.
species_range_compression.caption: An American pika on Flattop Mountain in Rocky Mountain National Park. This mountain species provides context for habitat-range pressure; one sighting does not show a range change.
species_range_compression.credit: Miguel Vieira from Redwood City, CA, USA

insurance_retreat.alt: An abandoned kitchen has stained floors, peeling lower walls and damaged doorways.
insurance_retreat.caption: A flood-damaged kitchen in New Orleans’ Hollygrove neighbourhood, in a house later demolished. Physical housing damage provides context for insurance exposure, not evidence of a policy decision.

adaptation_capital_shortfall.alt: A construction worker walks through dense reinforcement bars inside a large concrete culvert.
adaptation_capital_shortfall.caption: A worker carries timber through flood-control box culverts under construction at Napa Creek, California. Adaptation projects require funding and labour; a financing shortfall is not depicted.
adaptation_capital_shortfall.credit: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers Sacramento District

methane_hydroxyl_sink_loss.alt: Sunlight passes through the transparent curved walls of a large atmospheric-chemistry research chamber.
methane_hydroxyl_sink_loss.caption: The SAPHIR chamber at Forschungszentrum Jülich supports controlled research on atmospheric degradation of trace gases. Laboratory chemistry provides context for the atmosphere’s hydroxyl cleaning capacity.

wastewater_bypass_discharge.alt: A pale effluent plume spreads from a riverside facility into dark river water.
wastewater_bypass_discharge.caption: An archival EPA photograph shows a visible sewage discharge into the Niagara River. It illustrates receiving-water exposure; a specific treatment-bypass event is not established by the image.

oceanic_deoxygenation.alt: Researchers draw water from a rack of grey sampling bottles aboard a research ship.
oceanic_deoxygenation.caption: Technicians Marnie Jo Zirbel and Jonathan Whitefield collect samples for carbon and dissolved-oxygen analysis aboard R/V Sikuliaq during the Endurance 14 cruise. Sampling reveals conditions invisible at the surface.
oceanic_deoxygenation.credit: Ed Dever / Oregon State University, Ocean Observatories Initiative

atlantic_ni_o_ni_a.alt: A weathered red-and-black monitoring buoy with a metal instrument mast floats in choppy water.
atlantic_ni_o_ni_a.caption: A PIRATA monitoring buoy at 0° latitude, 0° longitude in the equatorial Atlantic, photographed in 2017. Ocean observations help track tropical Atlantic variability.

coastal_hypoxia.alt: A coastal lagoon lies between low scrub, sand and distant hills.
coastal_hypoxia.caption: Pescadero Lagoon, California, photographed in 2012. US Fish and Wildlife Service documents fish-kill risks linked to low inflow, loss of oxygen-rich surface water and hydrogen sulfide; those chemical conditions are not visible here.
coastal_hypoxia.credit: Sarah Swenty / US Fish and Wildlife Service

littoral_surge_vulnerability.alt: Floodwater surrounds palms and road signs in a coastal park during Hurricane Idalia.
littoral_surge_vulnerability.caption: Hurricane Idalia’s storm surge inundates Flora Wylie Park in St. Petersburg, Florida, in 2023. Water covers normally accessible coastal land around trees and road signs.

surface_water_withdrawal_pressure.alt: Concrete gates split flowing river water between a channel and an irrigation diversion.
surface_water_withdrawal_pressure.caption: The Montrose and Delta Diversion Dam diverts water from Colorado’s Uncompahgre River into an irrigation canal. The structure illustrates managed surface-water withdrawal.

land_use_fire_co2.alt: A farmer holds a long stick beside flames consuming dry branches on agricultural land.
land_use_fire_co2.caption: A farmer manages a fire to clear dry vegetation on farmland in Nigeria in March 2025. Burning vegetation releases carbon dioxide; the photograph shows the land-clearing activity, not an emissions measurement.

industrial_heat_decarbonization_gap.alt: A furnace interior glows orange above dark blocks, with blue burner flames along its floor.
industrial_heat_decarbonization_gap.caption: Inside an industrial furnace lined with high-temperature insulation. The intense heat illustrates the industrial processes that need lower-carbon heat sources.

rain_on_snow_flood_risk.alt: A torrent pours through a broken concrete spillway and gouges a rocky hillside.
rain_on_snow_flood_risk.caption: Water rushes over the damaged Oroville Dam spillway in February 2017. This is flood-infrastructure context; the photograph alone does not establish a rain-on-snow contribution.
rain_on_snow_flood_risk.credit: William Croyle, California Department of Water Resources

coastal_property_insurance_redlines.alt: A severely tilted house with exposed framing bears a spray-painted request not to demolish it.
coastal_property_insurance_redlines.caption: A house swept off its foundations in New Orleans after Hurricane Katrina. Physical property damage illustrates the exposure behind coastal insurance risk, without establishing this property's insurance status.

shipping_lane_disruption.alt: A large container ship lies diagonally across a narrow canal between a built-up bank and desert.
shipping_lane_disruption.caption: A Sentinel-2 satellite photograph of Ever Given blocking the Suez Canal on 24 March 2021. The natural-colour image was processed by Pierre Markuse from Copernicus data.
shipping_lane_disruption.credit: Contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data [2021], processed by Pierre Markuse

overstory_tree_mortality.alt: Tall bare spruce trunks rise above dense green saplings, with fallen dead wood on the forest floor.
overstory_tree_mortality.caption: Dead spruce trees stand above living young trees near the summit of Großer Falkenstein in the Bavarian Forest National Park. The contrast makes the loss of the upper canopy visible; the photograph alone does not identify its cause or rate.

resource_depletion.alt: Repeated mining benches descend into a huge open pit carved into an arid landscape.
resource_depletion.caption: The vast terraced excavation at Chile's Chuquicamata copper mine, photographed in 2016. It shows the physical scale of mineral extraction, rather than a measurement of remaining reserves.

grid_peak_load_stress.alt: An electricity dispatcher operates a broad control desk covered in switches and load indicators.
grid_peak_load_stress.caption: An electricity dispatcher balances loads at Yokosuka in March 2011, during power shortages following the Tohoku earthquake and Fukushima disaster. This documents emergency grid operations rather than a measurement of peak demand.
grid_peak_load_stress.credit: U.S. Navy photo by Joe Schmitt

mortgage_market_exposure.alt: Houses and surrounding roads are inundated by brown floodwater.
mortgage_market_exposure.caption: Houses beside the Mississippi south of Clarksville, Missouri, stand in floodwater in June 2008. The scene shows physical exposure of housing used as mortgage collateral; individual loan and insurance arrangements are not shown.

estuarine_nursery_loss.alt: A long silver fish rests in shallow water between looping mangrove roots and green leaves.
estuarine_nursery_loss.caption: A barracuda shelters among mangrove roots in shallow water. The photograph shows habitat whose loss can disrupt estuarine food webs; it does not show a measured loss event.

coal_industrial_heat_co2.alt: Workers in colourful shirts stack and move rows of bricks inside a brick kiln.
coal_industrial_heat_co2.caption: Workers stack sun-dried bricks at a kiln in Bangladesh before coal firing, as documented by the photographer. Brick production illustrates an industrial use of coal heat.

iron_steel_process_co2.alt: A brilliant white-orange flame erupts from a tilted steel converter amid dark industrial framing.
iron_steel_process_co2.caption: Molten iron is blown in a Bessemer converter at Republic Steel in Youngstown, Ohio, in 1941. This archival photograph shows a steelmaking process that removes carbon from iron.

amoc.alt: Researchers in survival gear guide a large yellow ocean profiler over a research ship’s rail.
amoc.caption: Researchers deploy a wire-following profiler in the Irminger Sea. Measurements in this North Atlantic deep-water formation region help observe ocean circulation; the photograph does not show an AMOC trend.
amoc.credit: Bob Weller / WHOI, Ocean Observatories Initiative

subpolar_gyre_weakening.alt: A yellow winged underwater glider floats at the surface of a dark, rippled sea.
subpolar_gyre_weakening.caption: An ocean-observing glider awaits its first dive in the Irminger Sea in 2015. Such measurements sample the subpolar North Atlantic; weakening of its circulation requires a time series.
subpolar_gyre_weakening.credit: Sheri N. White / Ocean Observatories Initiative

shelf_sea_hypoxia.alt: An instrument platform hangs in blue seawater with sunlight filtering down from above.
shelf_sea_hypoxia.caption: The Oregon Slope Base Shallow Profiler measures dissolved oxygen, nutrients and other seawater properties below the surface. These observations help detect conditions that cannot be judged from the sea's appearance.
shelf_sea_hypoxia.credit: NSF-OOI / University of Washington / ISS, VISIONS 2015

ocean_carbon_uptake_weakening.alt: A bundled-up researcher caps a sample bottle beside a rack of seawater samples on a research ship.
ocean_carbon_uptake_weakening.caption: Marnie Jo Zirbel seals a seawater sample in a shipboard wet lab. The samples are stored for dissolved inorganic carbon analysis, one part of observing the ocean carbon cycle.

pacific_decadal_oscillation.alt: Crew members guide a large orange instrument float over the stern of a research vessel.
pacific_decadal_oscillation.caption: A research crew deploys a profiler-mooring float at Station Papa in the northeast Pacific. Sustained observations help track ocean variability over time.
pacific_decadal_oscillation.credit: Station Papa Science Team / Ocean Observatories Initiative

thermal_stratification_intensification.alt: A cylindrical water-sampling rack hangs above the ocean beneath a blue dawn sky.
thermal_stratification_intensification.caption: A conductivity, temperature and depth sampler is lowered from R/V Sikuliaq during the Endurance 18 cruise. Profiles reveal how strongly water is layered with depth.
thermal_stratification_intensification.credit: Jon Fram / Oregon State University, Ocean Observatories Initiative

passenger_road_fuel_co2.alt: Long queues of cars and trucks fill a motorway beneath overhead route signs.
passenger_road_fuel_co2.caption: Evening rush-hour traffic on the A12 near Gouda, the Netherlands. Vehicle activity provides context for passenger-road fuel use and emissions.

rainforest_savannization.alt: Lines of fire and tall smoke plumes cut across a forested landscape seen obliquely from space.
rainforest_savannization.caption: Forest-clearing fires along Brazil's Rio Xingu, photographed by the ISS Expedition 29 crew. Burning and forest loss are pressures that can push moist rainforest toward a drier, more open landscape.

fossil_hydrogen_co2.alt: Tall process towers, pipes and chimneys stand across a fenced industrial site.
fossil_hydrogen_co2.caption: Linde's steam methane reformer at the Leuna chemical site in Germany. This facility illustrates hydrogen production using a fossil feedstock.

delta_salt_intrusion_fronts.alt: A person in a conical hat sits in a small wooden boat on a wide, sunlit river.
delta_salt_intrusion_fronts.caption: A small boat on the Mekong Delta's waterways at Phong Điền, Vietnam. It shows a river-dependent setting exposed to changing saltwater intrusion; salinity itself is invisible.

carbon_monoxide.alt: A white wall-mounted carbon monoxide alarm displays a red digital reading.
carbon_monoxide.caption: A carbon monoxide alarm monitors an invisible gas. Its displayed reading is local to this photograph and does not describe outdoor air or a current TULIP score.

freshwater_lens_compression.alt: A woman pushes a cart carrying a bucket of drinking water along a path beside homes.
freshwater_lens_compression.caption: A Tuvalu resident carries water home from a public collection point established during the 2011 drought. Limited island freshwater storage makes reliable drinking-water supplies vulnerable.
freshwater_lens_compression.credit: Australian Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade

green_steel.alt: Tall reactor buildings, platforms and process equipment at the HYBRIT hydrogen-based ironmaking pilot plant.
green_steel.caption: HYBRIT’s pilot direct-reduction plant in Luleå, Sweden, tests hydrogen in place of coal to reduce iron ore for steelmaking. This is a documented production facility; its exterior does not demonstrate a measured lifecycle emissions value.

arctic_amplification_rates.alt: A researcher in a red survival suit holds a light-measuring instrument over a dark melt pond.
arctic_amplification_rates.caption: Don Perovich measures reflected sunlight over Chukchi Sea ice and melt ponds during NASA's ICESCAPE campaign in July 2011. Reduced reflectivity is one mechanism involved in Arctic amplification.

desertification_frontiers.alt: A fence separates nearly bare, degraded grazing land from denser grassland.
desertification_frontiers.caption: Overgrazing and drought have left sparse vegetation on one side of this South Dakota fence, beside a healthier plant community. The contrast illustrates land degradation; one photograph does not establish the rate or global extent of desertification.

conflict_risk_escalation.alt: People stand beside rubble and a shattered apartment block with collapsed balconies and missing windows.
conflict_risk_escalation.caption: Visitors beside a bomb-damaged apartment building in Izium, Ukraine, photographed in December 2022 after the March attack. This documents civilian harm from armed conflict; it does not attribute the war to climate change.

madden_julian_oscillation.alt: Dark storm clouds gather over tropical houses, palms and a grassy open area.
madden_julian_oscillation.caption: An evening storm over Darwin, Australia, in 1971. Tropical rainfall is affected by large-scale variability including the Madden–Julian Oscillation; the phase of that pattern cannot be identified from one storm photograph.

trade_wind_weakening.alt: Puffy white clouds stretch above a turquoise ocean beyond low coastal vegetation.
trade_wind_weakening.caption: Trade-wind clouds above Sand Island at Midway Atoll, photographed in 2017. The scene illustrates the Pacific wind regime, without indicating a measured weakening.

cooling_water_competition.alt: White water pours from a coastal power-station outfall beside concrete sea defences.
cooling_water_competition.caption: Cooling water returns to the sea at Torness power station. Power-station cooling links electricity generation to water availability and discharge conditions.

high_altitude_forest_shrinkage.alt: A person in a red jacket plants a young tree on a steep rocky mountain slope.
high_altitude_forest_shrinkage.caption: Planting a native Polylepis tree in Llaca, Peru. Restoring high-altitude woodland provides context for the mountain forests at risk.

food_import_exposure.alt: A blue and red grain ship moors below tall grain silos and unloading equipment.
food_import_exposure.caption: A grain ship unloads beside a waterfront mill. Imported staples depend on ports, shipping and reliable overseas supply.

telecom_backbone.alt: A technician in a hard hat guides cable from a large reel into an underground conduit.
telecom_backbone.caption: Technicians install underground fibre-optic cable in 2025. These physical cables form part of the communications infrastructure exposed to disruption.
telecom_backbone.credit: U.S. Air Force photo by Senior Airman Grace Turpin

cattle_grazing_overcompaction.alt: A group of shaggy cattle stands in churned mud beside a fence and hay feeder.
cattle_grazing_overcompaction.caption: Highland cattle stand on heavily trampled, muddy ground. Repeated hoof traffic can compact wet pasture soils.

aerosolized_microplastics.alt: A metal spoon holds many tiny coloured plastic fragments against a pale background.
aerosolized_microplastics.caption: Microplastic fragments photographed on a spoon. This close-up shows the material; airborne particles are much smaller and are not shown suspended in air.

snowpack_dust_soot_coverage.alt: A cut face of snow reveals distinct yellow-brown dust bands between white layers.
snowpack_dust_soot_coverage.caption: A brown layer of Saharan dust is exposed within snow at Simplon Pass. Dark deposits reduce the reflectivity of snow.

urban_hydrologic_supply_shortfall.alt: A blue water tanker is parked beside an apartment building with a delivery hose attached.
urban_hydrologic_supply_shortfall.caption: A private tanker delivers water to a building in Chennai in 2017. Tanker supply is one way cities supplement their piped water systems.

volatile_organic_compounds.alt: A worker wearing a face covering directs a spray gun at a white vehicle body.
volatile_organic_compounds.caption: A worker spray-paints a vehicle body. Coating and solvent use can release volatile organic compounds; this photograph shows the activity, not the paint formulation or the concentration of invisible gases.

sulfur_dioxide.alt: Two researchers stand among pale gas plumes on the rocky rim of a volcanic crater.
sulfur_dioxide.caption: INGV researchers sample volcanic gases at Vulcano, Italy. Volcanic emissions are a natural source of sulfur dioxide; the visible plume also contains water vapour.

fish_landing_supply_disruption.alt: A large fishing boat rests tilted on dry land as people walk past.
fish_landing_supply_disruption.caption: A fishing boat was carried ashore by the 2010 Chile tsunami at Talcahuano. Damage to vessels and ports can interrupt fish landings; this event was caused by an earthquake.

cement_process_emissions.alt: A metal pail holds rough grey lumps of cement clinker.
cement_process_emissions.caption: Clinker from the Superior Portland Cement Company, displayed at the Concrete Heritage Museum. Producing this cement ingredient releases carbon dioxide when limestone is calcined.

acid_rain_deposition.alt: A carved stone figure has severely worn facial features and pitted surfaces.
acid_rain_deposition.caption: A weathered stone monument documented by its photographer as damaged by acid rain.

trophic_cascade_collapses.alt: A sea otter floats on its back with food held against its chest.
trophic_cascade_collapses.caption: A sea otter eats a clam off San Mateo County, California. Predators such as otters connect food-web relationships; this photograph does not document a cascade collapse.

aquifer_overdraft.alt: An old irrigation well and wooden lifting structure stand beside green fields at sunset.
aquifer_overdraft.caption: A traditional well supplies surrounding farmland. Aquifer overdraft occurs when sustained groundwater withdrawal exceeds replenishment; a single photograph cannot establish that balance.

supply_chain_port_bottlenecks.alt: Rows of tall container cranes rise above ships and stacks of freight containers.
supply_chain_port_bottlenecks.caption: Container cranes and stacked cargo at Hamburg harbour. Concentrating freight through terminals makes supply chains sensitive to port disruption.

peat_oxidation_pulse.alt: An exposed dark peat bank crosses open moorland beside bags of cut peat.
peat_oxidation_pulse.caption: Peat cutting in Shetland exposes dark organic soil to air. Draining and disturbing peat can accelerate oxidation and carbon release.

antarctic_bottom_water_decline.alt: People wearing red parkas walk across snow-covered sea ice beside open water.
antarctic_bottom_water_decline.caption: People cross sea ice in the Weddell Sea, Antarctica. This region contributes to dense bottom-water formation; the photograph provides geographic context, not a measurement of its decline.

walker_circulation_shift.alt: A small workboat and buoy are silhouetted against a glittering sea beneath dark clouds.
walker_circulation_shift.caption: NOAA buoy riders service a Tropical Atmosphere Ocean buoy. The Pacific observing network helps researchers track coupled ocean and atmospheric circulation.

arctic_oscillation.alt: Parked cars almost disappear beneath deep snow on a Washington street.
arctic_oscillation.caption: Cars buried during the February 2010 blizzard in Washington, DC. NOAA documented a record negative Arctic Oscillation that month as one contributor to the circulation pattern; the snowfall was also shaped by other weather drivers.

nighttime_heat_retention.alt: Illuminated signs and tall buildings line a busy city street at night.
nighttime_heat_retention.caption: Shinjuku after dark. Dense buildings and paved streets provide context for the urban surfaces that store daytime heat and release it at night.

cooling_equity_gaps.alt: A low public recreation building stands beneath a clear sky beside a residential street.
cooling_equity_gaps.caption: A New Orleans recreation building operated as a cooling centre during the hot summer of 2023. Access to places like this matters when households cannot cool their homes.

heatwave_excess_mortality_rates.alt: Medics support a woman receiving urgent treatment after collapsing from heatstroke.
heatwave_excess_mortality_rates.caption: Medics assist a woman who collapsed from heatstroke in Zacapa, Guatemala, in 2014. This documents treatment for serious heat illness, not a death or a population mortality estimate.

heat_related_mortality_burden.alt: A patient lies on a stretcher while medics check his condition and provide treatment.
heat_related_mortality_burden.caption: Army medics treat a soldier for heat exhaustion at Fort Irwin, California, in 2012. The scene illustrates the health burden of heat; it does not depict a fatality.

low_carbon_cement.alt: Gloved fingers hold a small grey material sample filled with round pores.
low_carbon_cement.caption: A researcher holds a porous geopolymer sample. Geopolymers are investigated as alternatives to conventional cement-based materials; the photograph does not quantify this sample's carbon footprint.
low_carbon_cement.credit: Eva Santini, Michela E. Pedretti, Giovanna Canu, CNR-ICMATE

coastal_inundation_risk.alt: Maintenance vehicles drive through floodwater surrounding coastal buildings.
coastal_inundation_risk.caption: King-tide ocean overwash floods the National Park Service maintenance area at Great Island Cabin Camp in 2019.

atmospheric_dryness.alt: Green leaves hang limp from the branches of a shrub above dry ground.
atmospheric_dryness.caption: A forsythia wilts during a dry spell in New Jersey in June 2023. Plant water stress provides visible context for drying conditions; atmospheric humidity is not measured in this image.

pelagic_species_redistribution.alt: Many yellow-finned tuna swim together through deep blue water.
pelagic_species_redistribution.caption: A school of yellowfin tuna gathered by a seine net off the Seychelles, photographed by Ifremer. Mobile ocean fish are sensitive to their thermal habitat; one school does not demonstrate a range shift.

fisheries_range_redistribution.alt: Several silver Spanish mackerel lie closely packed in a metal basin.
fisheries_range_redistribution.caption: Narrow-barred Spanish mackerel landed in Chanthaburi, Thailand. Changes in fish distribution affect what fisheries can catch; this image identifies the species, not a measured range change.

shell_calcification_failures.alt: Tall experimental enclosures stand in a fjord as researchers work from a small boat beneath snowy mountains.
shell_calcification_failures.caption: Scientists sample experimental enclosures in Svalbard to study marine organisms' responses to ocean acidification. This is a field experiment, not a photograph of damaged shells.

staple_food_price_volatility.alt: Two campaigners hold oversized playing cards and a roulette wheel reading Stop banks betting on hunger.
staple_food_price_volatility.caption: Campaigners in Birmingham, October 2012, protest financial speculation in food prices. Their signs make a food-affordability concern explicit; the scene documents advocacy, not a measured price change.

asphalt_pavement_heat_absorbers.alt: A heavy roller flattens a strip of freshly laid asphalt beside a kerb.
asphalt_pavement_heat_absorbers.caption: A road roller compacts fresh asphalt at Chièvres, Belgium, in 2021. Dark paved surfaces absorb solar energy and store heat.
asphalt_pavement_heat_absorbers.credit: U.S. Army photo by Henri Cambier

chemical_process_co2.alt: A worker tends glowing furnace openings beneath enormous bundles of electrical cables in a chemical plant.
chemical_process_co2.caption: A worker tends an electric phosphate-smelting furnace making elemental phosphorus at a TVA chemical plant in Alabama, photographed in June 1942. The operating furnace shows chemical production at industrial scale; emissions depend on process chemistry and energy supply.
chemical_process_co2.credit: Alfred T. Palmer / U.S. Office of War Information / Library of Congress

soil_humus_decline.alt: Hands hold a block of soil with grass roots and old plant material while another hand points to its structure.
soil_humus_decline.caption: A soil sample from hayground rested the previous year at Ray Banister Ranch, Montana, in June 2020. The retained old grass protects soil carbon during drought. This illustrates the organic cover at stake, rather than measuring humus loss.

gulf_stream_slowdown.alt: Clouds trace the Florida peninsula beside deep-blue ocean and the turquoise shallows of the Bahamas.
gulf_stream_slowdown.caption: Florida, the Bahamas and the deep-blue Gulf Stream photographed from Space Shuttle Atlantis in 1992. This shows the current’s geographic setting, not a measurement of changing flow.

agricultural_soil_compaction.alt: Deep parallel tractor ruts hold brown standing water across a grassy field.
agricultural_soil_compaction.caption: Water collects in deep tractor ruts near Falla, Scotland. Visible soil deformation provides context for machinery compaction and impaired infiltration; no soil-density measurement is shown.

black_carbon_deposition.alt: A dark soot stain spreads across a silver truck body above its engine compartment.
black_carbon_deposition.caption: Black soot stains the body of a refrigerated truck in Lille, France. The deposit makes particulate pollution from combustion visible on a surface.

semiconductor_fabrication_footprint.alt: Researchers in protective cleanroom suits work at processing stations under amber lighting.
semiconductor_fabrication_footprint.caption: Researchers work in a photolithography cleanroom at the London Centre for Nanotechnology. Chip fabrication relies on tightly controlled environments, chemicals, energy and purified water.
semiconductor_fabrication_footprint.credit: UCL Mathematical & Physical Sciences from London, UK

stratospheric_chlorine_sinks.alt: The low sun shines through the curved glass dome of an ozone-monitoring instrument.
stratospheric_chlorine_sinks.caption: Early sunlight through the optical dome of Manchester’s Brewer ozone and ultraviolet spectrophotometer. Instruments like this monitor the ozone layer from the ground.

nocturnal_heat_stress.alt: A metal fan rests on bedding beside a pillow in a room lit by warm evening light.
nocturnal_heat_stress.caption: A fan sits on a bed in a dimly lit room. The scene provides context for overnight cooling and rest; no room temperature or heat illness is documented.

groundwater_depletion.alt: A hand holds a metal groundwater logger beside an open monitoring well.
groundwater_depletion.caption: A groundwater monitoring instrument at Coronado National Memorial, Arizona. Such measurements track aquifer levels; this photograph does not establish depletion at this site.

nutrient_pollution.alt: Green algal streaks cover the surface of river water.
nutrient_pollution.caption: Green algal growth on the Dnipro in Dnipro city, photographed in August 2026. Visible eutrophication illustrates the effects associated with excess nutrients.

atlantic_multidecadal_oscillation.alt: A yellow ocean-observing buoy with a tall instrument tower floats in the North Atlantic.
atlantic_multidecadal_oscillation.caption: An Ocean Observatories Initiative buoy in the Irminger Sea after deployment in 2015. Long-term ocean observations help study North Atlantic climate variability; a single photograph cannot show the oscillation.
atlantic_multidecadal_oscillation.credit: Sheri N. White / Ocean Observatories Initiative

coastal_groundwater_withdrawal.alt: Rows of strawberries stretch toward the horizon beside two water-management specialists.
coastal_groundwater_withdrawal.caption: Water-management specialists visit a Pajaro Valley strawberry farm in 2015. The coastal valley relies heavily on groundwater and uses recycled water and recharge to reduce pressure on its aquifer.

aviation_demand_growth.alt: Several passenger jets wait in a line beside an airport runway.
aviation_demand_growth.caption: Passenger aircraft queue for take-off. The photograph illustrates aviation activity; growth in demand is established from traffic data.
aviation_demand_growth.credit: Charles from Port Chester, New York

gas_industrial_heat_co2.alt: Purple gas flames heat a glowing pipe elbow inside an industrial machine.
gas_industrial_heat_co2.caption: Gas flames heat pipe for forming at Tube Turns in Louisville, Kentucky, in 1941. This historical photograph shows gas-fired industrial process heat.

firn_layer_depletion.alt: Two researchers measure layers in the tall white walls of a glacier snow pit.
firn_layer_depletion.caption: Researchers record snow layers in a pit on Sperry Glacier. Snow and firn measurements help assess glacier water storage; the photograph does not itself show declining storage capacity.

snow_drought.alt: Bare brown mountain slopes and scattered conifers under a clear blue winter sky.
snow_drought.caption: Snow-free slopes at Lassen Volcanic National Park during California’s January 2014 drought. The park documented unusually spring-like winter conditions.

solar_radiation_trapping.alt: A thin blue and orange atmospheric band curves above Earth against black space.
solar_radiation_trapping.caption: Earth’s atmosphere illuminated at sunset, photographed from the International Space Station in May 2024. Atmospheric context: greenhouse-gas radiative forcing cannot be seen in this photograph.

municipal_groundwater_withdrawal.alt: A municipal groundwater pumping station stands below a wooded hillside.
municipal_groundwater_withdrawal.caption: The Langau groundwater pumping station operated by Stadtwerke Kitzbühel, Austria. Municipal wells supply water from underground aquifers.

industrial_groundwater_withdrawal.alt: Large pipes lie beside excavated ground at a mine dewatering pipeline.
industrial_groundwater_withdrawal.caption: Groundwater-pumping pipeline at the Hambach open-pit mine in Germany. Mine dewatering is an industrial withdrawal of groundwater.

environ_anomalies.alt: Brown and green land across Britain is visible below the International Space Station.
environ_anomalies.caption: Britain photographed from the International Space Station during the August 2022 heatwave and drought. The image provides context for heat and water stress occurring together.

relocation_governance_capacity.alt: People in hard hats walk between newly built houses on a treeless coastal relocation site.
relocation_governance_capacity.caption: A visit to new housing construction at Mertarvik, Alaska, in 2019. Families from Newtok were relocating to the site because of coastal erosion; this shows a tangible relocation project.
relocation_governance_capacity.credit: United States Senate - Office of Lisa Murkowski

urban_water_rationing_zones.alt: An empty outdoor wading pool is closed off with yellow tape.
urban_water_rationing_zones.caption: An empty wading pool in Vancouver’s Grays Park during water restrictions in summer 2015.

nitrogen_fertilizer_runoff.alt: Muddy irrigation runoff and plant debris collect at a drainage culvert.
nitrogen_fertilizer_runoff.caption: Irrigation return runoff collects at a blocked culvert near Billings, Montana. Agricultural drainage can transport unused nutrients; their concentration is not visible in a photograph.

soot_deposition_on_snow.alt: Gray-streaked glacier ice borders rocky land and turquoise meltwater lakes in a Landsat image.
soot_deposition_on_snow.caption: Darkened ice along Greenland’s southwestern ice-sheet margin in August 2025. NASA attributes the gray surface to accumulated particles including black carbon and dust; this view does not isolate soot from other impurities.
soot_deposition_on_snow.credit: Wanmei Liang / NASA Earth Observatory; Landsat data: USGS

indian_ocean_dipole.alt: Crew members guide a suspended ocean-observing buoy over the side of a research ship at dusk.
indian_ocean_dipole.caption: A RAMA buoy is deployed from R/V Sagar Kanya in the Indian Ocean. These observing stations collect ocean and weather measurements used to study variability including the Indian Ocean Dipole.

cfc_saturated_layers.alt: A laboratory worker wearing safety glasses connects a row of blue air-sampling flasks to analysis equipment.
cfc_saturated_layers.caption: Molly Heller prepares air-sampling flasks at NOAA’s atmospheric laboratory in Boulder. The samples are analysed for greenhouse and ozone-depleting gases; CFC concentrations cannot be seen in a photograph.

reef_structural_collapse.alt: A diver’s hand holds a broken coral colony underwater above the sediment-covered reef.
reef_structural_collapse.caption: A diver holds coral dislodged by Hurricane Irma in Florida Keys National Marine Sanctuary. NOAA’s surveys documented broken corals and fractures in the reef framework after the storm.

temp.alt: Earth seen from space, with Africa and cloud bands above the southern oceans against black space.
temp.caption: The Apollo 17 crew photographed the sunlit Earth on 7 December 1972. This view shows the planet as a whole; global mean temperature is calculated from observations across land and ocean, not from a photograph.
temp.credit: NASA Johnson Space Center / Apollo 17 crew

ambient_air_quality_deficit.alt: Solar panels and air-sampling equipment stand beside dry grass and trees at a monitoring station in Beirut.
ambient_air_quality_deficit.caption: An air-quality monitoring station in Horsh Beirut. Such instruments measure pollutants that may be invisible; the surrounding view does not establish whether the air is safe.

arctic_pack_ice_drift.alt: A jagged ridge of piled sea ice stretches across a snowy Arctic surface beside an expedition tent.
arctic_pack_ice_drift.caption: Pressure ridges in Arctic pack ice at the North Pole, photographed in April 1990. These ridges form as moving ice floes converge; the photograph does not measure drift speed.

rossby_wave_stalling.alt: Rows of white clouds curve around a broad clear area over the eastern United States.
rossby_wave_stalling.caption: Cloud streets curve around a high-pressure ridge over the eastern United States in September 2010. This satellite view illustrates atmospheric circulation, not evidence that a Rossby wave was stalled.
rossby_wave_stalling.credit: NASA image by Jeff Schmaltz, MODIS Rapid Response Team at NASA GSFC. Caption by Michael Carlowicz, with interpretation help from Tom Arnold of NASA GSFC.

southern_annular_mode.alt: White cloud bands spiral around a large Southern Ocean storm above dark blue water.
southern_annular_mode.caption: A powerful Southern Ocean cyclone observed by GOES-16 in October 2022. This visible-light satellite view provides storm-track context for the Southern Annular Mode; a single cyclone does not establish its phase.

fracking_wastewater_lakes.alt: A large rectangular water pond lined with black plastic sits inside a fenced natural-gas drilling site.
fracking_wastewater_lakes.caption: A lined water impoundment at a Marcellus Shale natural-gas drilling site in southwestern Pennsylvania. This illustrates on-site water containment; the source does not identify the stored water’s composition or document a leak.

nitrous_oxide.alt: A tractor tows a tall manure spreader across a muddy farm field.
nitrous_oxide.caption: Manure spreading at Angelrow Farm. Microbial processing of nitrogen in fertilised soils and manure can release nitrous oxide; the gas itself is invisible.

anoxic_dead_zones.alt: Thin green phytoplankton bands spiral through dark seawater in a Landsat view of the Gulf of Oman.
anoxic_dead_zones.caption: Phytoplankton swirls in the Gulf of Oman in March 2025. When dense blooms decay, bacteria can consume oxygen and contribute to hypoxia; the satellite image shows the bloom, not dissolved oxygen levels.
anoxic_dead_zones.credit: Wanmei Liang / NASA Earth Observatory; Landsat data: USGS

blue_carbon_habitat_loss.alt: Tall bare trunks rise above dense green mangroves beneath a blue sky.
blue_carbon_habitat_loss.caption: Standing dead trunks among mangroves in Mexico’s Celestún Biosphere Reserve. Mangrove loss can reduce coastal carbon storage; this photograph does not identify the cause of tree death or quantify carbon released.
blue_carbon_habitat_loss.credit: Katja Schulz from Washington, D. C., USA

estuary_eutrophication.alt: Green bloom streaks spread across Lake Pontchartrain beside the New Orleans shoreline in a Landsat image.
estuary_eutrophication.caption: An algal bloom colours Lake Pontchartrain, part of Louisiana’s coastal estuary, in March 2018. Warm conditions and nutrient availability support blooms; satellite colour alone does not measure nutrient concentrations or toxicity.
estuary_eutrophication.credit: Joshua Stevens / NASA Earth Observatory; Landsat data: USGS

oceanic_upwelling_disruptions.alt: An electric-blue band of bioluminescent surf glows beneath dark coastal cliffs at night.
oceanic_upwelling_disruptions.caption: Bioluminescent Noctiluca lights the surf. Seasonal winds and upwelling can supply nutrients that support plankton blooms; this coastal photograph provides food-web context, not proof of disrupted upwelling.

marine_fisheries_collapse.alt: A fisher in a red life vest lifts a mesh fishing pot containing fish and crabs from the sea.
marine_fisheries_collapse.caption: A Newfoundland fisher hauls an experimental cod pot off Fogo Island in 2016. The photograph provides context for a fishery with a history of collapse; this catch does not establish the condition of the wider fish population.

commercial_gas_heat_co2.alt: Large boilers, insulated pipework and yellow supply pipes fill a high school’s mechanical room.
commercial_gas_heat_co2.caption: The boiler room of a public high school. Heating equipment provides context for fuel use in public and commercial buildings; the photograph does not quantify fuel consumption or CO2 emissions.

peatland_drainage_co2.alt: A narrow drainage ditch cuts through brown moorland toward distant hills.
peatland_drainage_co2.caption: An open drainage ditch crosses moorland above Glen Cassley in Scotland. Draining peat exposes carbon-rich material to air, allowing decomposition and CO2 release; those emissions are not visible.

methane_leak_detection.alt: A portable Dräger gas detector lies beside its metal sampling probe.
methane_leak_detection.caption: A portable multi-gas detector with a sampling probe. Instruments of this type can be configured to detect methane; finding a leak must be followed by repair and verification.

wildfire_smoke_hospitalization_burden.alt: A health professional in blue scrubs holds a clear nebulizer mask and tubing.
wildfire_smoke_hospitalization_burden.caption: A health professional prepares a nebulizer for respiratory treatment. This clinical photograph illustrates the care that breathing problems can require; it does not depict an identified wildfire-smoke patient.

urban_water_demand_peak.alt: A water tanker stands beneath a tall roadside refill pipe in Bengaluru.
urban_water_demand_peak.caption: A water tanker refills at a roadside supply point in Bengaluru in July 2024. The photograph shows urban water distribution, rather than a measured peak in demand.

humanitarian_access_constraints.alt: Aid vans and people gather beneath the gate at the Rafah border crossing.
humanitarian_access_constraints.caption: A British aid convoy enters the Gaza Strip from Egypt through the Rafah crossing in 2009. This photograph shows the border infrastructure humanitarian deliveries must navigate; it does not show a blocked convoy.
